title: writable gate's bash-redirect detection is quote-blind: '| tee f' inside a quoted python -c string is blocked as a real write
detail: Observed 2026-10-25 in solo_execute: a Bash command '.venv/bin/python -c "...print(s._statements(\"... ; echo ok | tee f\"))..."' was blocked with 'blocks bash redirect to f: f not in writable patterns' — the 'tee f' was inside a quoted Python string literal, never executed by the shell. The redirect detector scans raw text rather than shell-tokenized statements. Low severity (false block, fail-closed, easily rephrased) but it trains agents to rephrase around the gate. Suggest: tokenize with shlex(punctuation_chars) — the same quote-aware statement split schema._statements now uses — before looking for redirects/tee targets.
